v2_findings.title: EPLI — Wage & Hour Defense Sublimit
v2_findings.content:
[Bad] EPLI — Wage & Hour Defense Sublimit
Risk Score: 9/25

What this means:
If a former employee filed a wage and hour class action — a very common claim type — your insurance pays for $100K of defense costs and zero damages. The company manages its own defense (the carrier won't even appoint a lawyer). $100K is what one lawyer at a firm bills in three months on a class act

Recommendation:
Increase W&H defense sublimit to $250K-$500K at renewal. Audit timekeeping, exempt classifications, meal/rest break compliance especially in CA. Consider standalone wage & hour policy if exposure warr

v2_findings.title: D&O Entity Coverage — Manufacturing & Professional Services
v2_findings.content:
[Ugly] D&O Entity Coverage — Manufacturing & Professional Services 
Risk Score: 20/25

What this means:
Your D&O policy says: if a county sues your company because a ballot system failed or you didn't deliver election services correctly, the company itself is NOT covered. Only the individual directors and officers are covered, and only if shareholders sue. This is the worst possible exclusion for your

Recommendation:
Negotiate removal or material narrowing of PP 00 H350 at renewal. If carrier won't budge, secure standalone Tech E&O entity-level wrapper or place D&O with a different carrier that does not impose thi

v2_findings.title: PE Co-Defendant Extension on Management Liability
v2_findings.content:
[Good] PE Co-Defendant Extension on Management Liability

What this means:
Your PE owners (Lincoln Shields and Black Mountain) are protected by your D&O if someone sues them solely because they own you. Good. They probably also have their own insurance, but yours is a useful first line.

Recommendation:
Maintain. Verify named entities still match current ownership at each renewal.

Your D&O policy says you have $2 million of coverage. But for any wrongdoing that happened between mid-August 2023 and early April 2024, you actually only have $1 million.
